findings.text: EPT pointer table physical address occupies bits 51 through 12; comparison of cached roots uses only that masked portion.
A cached MMU root is treated as matching a candidate EPT pointer only when its host root is valid and the masked table bases are equal.

Address invalidation scans all previous MMU roots, collects those whose table base matches the supplied EPT pointer, and invalidates that address in the nested GPA walker for exactly that subset; caller is expected to be in nested MMU mode.

Nested EPT fault injection has three outcomes: pending PML full produces a PML full exit and clears the flag; reserved page fault error produces a misconfig exit with zero qualification; otherwise it produces a violation exit. Violation qualification preserves non address-info bits from the fault and takes address-info bits from hardware on hardware faults or from the synthesized fault otherwise, with extra user and permission info included only when the advanced exit info capability is present. It then invalidates matching cached roots and completes a nested exit while recording the faulting address.

Page fault interception compares masked error code against expected match and combines the inequality result with the page fault bitmap bit by exclusive or. Other vectors intercept exactly when their bitmap bit is set. Page fault checks use only the low 16 bits of the error code.

Effective nested MSR interception is the logical OR of the host owned bitmap and the L1 bitmap, computed separately for read and write directions. A helper merges one direction and a dispatcher applies read and write selectively according to requested type flags.

Shadow VMCS12 caching proceeds only when the shadow feature is enabled and the link pointer is valid. The GPA to host mapping is refreshed only when the link address changed and mapping setup succeeds, then a fixed size image is read from the guest into the shadow copy.

Copy from shadow VMCS to cached VMCS12 runs with preemption disabled across loading the shadow control structure, reading all readable and writable shadow fields into the cache, then clearing the shadow structure and restoring the previously loaded control structure.

A generic write into the cached VMCS12 selects store width from the field encoding among 16 bit, 32 bit, 64 bit and natural width, and stores the value at the supplied byte offset from the structure base; unknown widths are warned about and not stored.

Enlightened to cached VMCS12 synchronization always copies threshold and guest instruction pointer, then conditionally copies field groups only when the corresponding clean field bit is clear, covering enlightenment control identifiers, guest basics, processor and exception controls, entry controls and event data, host state, pin plus exit plus secondary controls, IO and MSR bitmap pointers, extended guest segment and table state, TSC and virtual APIC related controls, control register masks and guest control state, host pointers, translation controls, and guest group one. Missing runtime clean bits request MSR bitmap recalculation. Unsupported, absent and read only fields are skipped. Without Hyper-V support the path is treated as a bug.
On 64 bit hosts the exit control requesting host 64 bit address space must agree with the current long mode active state, otherwise nested entry preparation fails as invalid.

Nested state page preparation requires the enlightened page to be usable when that path applies and, when already in guest mode, requires VMCS12 pages to load successfully; failure in either step aborts preparation.

Nested PML logging expects guest mode and no preexisting full condition. It does nothing when PML is disabled for the nested guest, reports full and latches the full flag when the guest log index is exhausted, otherwise writes the page aligned address into the guest log slot addressed by base plus index and decrements the index; guest write failure leaves the index unchanged and reports no full event.

Nested VMX permission requires VMXON state, otherwise an undefined opcode exception is queued, and requires supervisor privilege, otherwise a general protection fault is injected; success returns an allowed indication.

Nested entry first checks permission and enlightened pointer state, accounts a branch event, then rejects invalid enlightened status, missing current pointer, and shadow VMCS targets. It synchronizes cached VMCS12 from the enlightened image with launch state derived from the requested operation, or from shadow VMCS when enabled, then rejects MOV SS blocking, launch state mismatch, invalid control fields and address space size mismatch before continuing.

Enlightened VMCLEAR handling declines when the guest lacks the enlightened capability or the enlightened pointer is invalid, releases the cached enlightened mapping only when the supplied address equals the currently cached enlightened address, and reports handled whenever enlightened operation is active; without Hyper-V support it always declines.

Because address translation caches associate entries with the table base rather than the full EPT pointer, fault handling must invalidate every cached root sharing the same base, not only the currently active pointer.
Exit qualification from hardware is valid only for hardware EPT violations; using it for synthesized faults, or ignoring it for hardware faults, would propagate stale or unrelated data.
